off.title: The device list is off
off.body: Turn on the Inventory module to view, declare and approve devices. Existing data is kept.

chip.fragileHint: Passive listening only, never actively scanned, so it does not hang.

list.meta: Every value shows its source and confidence. New values are added; old values are never overwritten.
list.titleBoxOnly: Only the Vedette box so far

table.caption: Device list
table.search: Search by name, IP, make, operating system

empty.manual: No device added by hand yet. Use "Add a device" to add one.

empty.title: No devices yet
empty.body: Plug the box into your LAN and Vedette finds devices by itself after about an hour. Or add devices by hand, or import a list from a CSV file.
empty.bodyNeutral: Devices appear here as the sensor hears them on the network, usually within an hour. Or add devices by hand, or import a list from a CSV file.
empty.bodyBoxOnlyNeutral: Only the Vedette box is on the list so far. Devices appear as the sensor hears them. You can also add devices by hand or import a CSV.
empty.bodyWatching: Vedette is watching the network ranges you saved. Devices appear here as the sensor hears them, usually within an hour. Or add devices by hand, or import a list from a CSV file.
empty.bodyBoxOnlyWatching: Only the Vedette box is on the list so far. Vedette is watching the network ranges you saved, and devices appear as the sensor hears them. You can also add devices by hand or import a CSV.
empty.bodyBoxOnly: Only the Vedette box is on the list so far. Add the other devices by hand, import a CSV, or give Vedette your network ranges so it finds them.

pending.description: A device seen on the network for the first time stays here until you approve it. If you do not recognise it, mark it unknown or remove it from the list (removing does not disconnect it).
pending.notifyOn: You will be notified about new devices.
pending.notifyVia: Notifications go through the channels you set up.
pending.notifyOff2: The Notifications module is off, so alerts cannot be sent yet.

delete.title: Remove {{name}} from the list?
delete.body: This only removes it from Vedette's inventory, not the real device. If it shows up on the network again it goes back to the not-approved list.
delete.findings_one: This device has {{count}} finding. Removing the device also removes that finding from the findings list; if the device shows up again it is assessed from scratch.
delete.findings_other: This device has {{count}} findings. Removing the device also removes those findings from the findings list; if the device shows up again it is assessed from scratch.

add.title: Add a device
add.body: Pick a product you use. Vedette alerts you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches it, even if the box is not plugged into your network yet.
add.versionHint: With the version, alerts are more precise. Leave empty if unknown.
add.name: Name (optional)
add.nameHint: A name you recognise, for example "Office firewall".
add.ipHint: Leave empty if unknown or the device is outside this network.
add.done: Added {{name}}. Vedette will alert you when an actively exploited vulnerability matches this product.
add.softwareBody: Pick software running on this device to get alerts that match it.
add.doneKev_one: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerability in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
add.doneKev_other: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerabilities in this product; Vedette will alert you when it matters.
add.softwareDoneKev_one: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerability in this software.
add.softwareDoneKev_other: Added {{name}}. Attackers have already exploited {{count}} vulnerabilities in this software.

picker.placeholder: Type a product, model or maker, for example FortiGate 60F
picker.hint: Type a product, maker or model, for example fortigate 60f or synology.
picker.none: No matching product. Try the maker (Fortinet, Synology) or another name, or enter it yourself below.
picker.kev_one: Exploited in real attacks before: {{count}} vulnerability
picker.kev_other: Exploited in real attacks before: {{count}} vulnerabilities
picker.notListed: Can't find it? Enter the maker and product yourself
picker.customNote: Vedette matches alerts by maker, so you still hear about exploited vulnerabilities in this maker's products even without an exact product match.
picker.more_one: {{count}} more match. Keep typing to narrow the list.
picker.more_other: {{count}} more matches. Keep typing to narrow the list.

import.title: Import devices from CSV
import.body: Use this when you already have a list in Excel. The first row must be column titles: name, ip, product, version, kind. At least name or product is needed. Wrong rows are reported by line number; correct rows are still added.
import.tooLarge: The file is larger than {{kb}} KB. Split it into smaller files and import them one by one.
import.notesHint: These rows were added. Check them:
import.errorsHint: Fix the rows below in your file and import again. Import only the fixed rows to avoid duplicates.

detail.title: {{name}}: {{kind}}, last seen {{when}}
detail.meta: Every observation is kept for comparison. For each field Vedette uses the value you entered; otherwise it ranks the sources: agent first, then SNMP, then scan or nmap, then passive listening. Within the same source the higher confidence wins, then the newest observation.
detail.fragileOnHint: Vedette scans this device gently once when it first sees it, then only listens (unless regular scans are allowed below).
detail.fragileOffHint: Vedette may scan this device during the scan window.
detail.origin: How it got on the list
detail.regularScanHint: After the first gentle scan, Vedette only listens to a fragile device or one of unknown type unless regular scans are allowed. Never means never, for every type of device.
detail.firstScanNone: No gentle first scan (declared by hand, the Vedette box itself, or a known type that is not fragile)

approval.pending: This device is not approved yet
approval.body: Approve it if you recognise it. Until then it is still tracked but stays in the waiting list.

obs.title: All observations
obs.description: Each time a sensor, a scan or you record a value, it is added here with its source and confidence.
obs.caption: Observations for this device

services.title: Open services
services.description: A normal scan replaces this list with the ports it found open. A gentle scan only adds ports, and a scan that timed out changes nothing. A port not seen for 90 days is removed.
services.caption: Services open on the device
services.name: Service
services.emptyBody: The active sensor has not scanned this device. Check the scan window in Scope and sensors.
services.emptyFragile: This is a fragile device, so Vedette scanned it gently once and only listens after that. Allow regular scans in the settings above if you want it checked again.

software.title: Software
software.description: The more exact the version, the more accurate the alerts.
software.caption: Software on the device
software.name: Software
software.emptyBody: Use "Add software" to say what runs on this device, or install an agent so Vedette reads it by itself.

notes.title: Notes
notes.label: Notes about the device
notes.placeholder: For example: in the accounting room, maintained by ABC company.

setup.meta: Vedette only listens and lightly scans inside the scope you set here. Vedette does not block traffic.
setup.forbidden: You do not have access to this page
setup.forbiddenBody: The {{role}} role is needed to change scan scope, sensors and agent tokens. Ask an administrator for access or to do it for you.

network.title: LAN ranges
network.description: Internal network ranges Vedette may actively scan. The passive sensor still hears everything it can see.
network.rangeHint: Use CIDR format with the prefix length, for example 192.168.10.0/24 or 192.168.10.0/25. Internal addresses only (10.x, 172.16 to 172.31, 192.168.x, 100.64 to 100.127).
network.noRanges: No ranges yet. Add at least one range to let Vedette scan.

problem.empty: Type a range first. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.noPrefix: "{{value}}" has no prefix length. Add it so Vedette scans the right size of network, for example {{value}}/24 or {{value}}/25.
problem.format: "{{value}}" is not a valid range. Write it like 192.168.10.0/24.
problem.hostBits: {{value}} is not written correctly: the address part must be the first address of the range. Use {{net}}.
problem.notPrivate: {{value}} is not an internal range, so it cannot be added here. To scan public addresses, use External exposure after verifying ownership.
problem.overlap: {{value}} overlaps {{other}}, which is already in the list. Keep the larger range and remove the smaller one.

note.network: {{from}} was added as {{to}}, the first address of its range.

network.fixFirst_one: Fix or remove the {{count}} range marked in red to save.
network.fixFirst_other: Fix or remove the {{count}} ranges marked in red to save.

active.title: Active scanning
active.description: A light scan to learn open ports and software versions. It runs only inside the time window below and only in the ranges above.
active.off: Active scanning is off, so Vedette only listens passively. Turn on the Active sensor module to learn open ports and versions.
active.crossMidnight: If the end time is earlier than the start (for example 23:00 to 05:00) the window runs past midnight. Pick hours when few people use the network.
active.rateHint: Slower is safer for old devices.
active.exclusionsHint: Devices or ranges never actively scanned, for example production machines or medical devices. Enter an IP or range and press Add.
active.badExclusion: Enter one IP (192.168.10.10) or a valid range (192.168.10.0/28, where the address part is the first address of the range).
active.safety: Active scanning only probes ports and reads versions. No exploitation, no denial of service.

fragile.title: Device types scanned only once
fragile.description: Vedette scans these gently once when it first sees them, then only listens. A device of unknown type is treated the same until it is classified.
fragile.note: Each device gets one scan at the lowest speed. To allow regular scans, switch it on for the type below. You can still change a single device on its detail page; changes here apply to devices you have not changed individually.

scope.title: Confirm the scope
scope.confirm: I confirm these network ranges belong to my company and I am allowed to scan them.
scope.notConfirmed: Not confirmed yet. Active scanning can only be saved after you confirm the ranges.
scope.asIs: Vedette is provided as is. Its author is not responsible for how you use it, including scanning.
scope.rangesChanged: You added or changed ranges. Tick to confirm before saving.
scope.willConfirm: Will be recorded as confirmed by you when you save.

sensors.title: Sensor on this box
sensors.description: The sensor listens to the network (DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP, LLDP) to learn devices without scanning. The port it listens on and SPAN are set in Settings → Box network.
sensors.descriptionNoSpan: The sensor listens to the network (DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP, LLDP) to learn devices without scanning. It listens on the box's management port, set in Settings → Box network.
sensors.descriptionContainerNoSpan: The sensor listens to the network (DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP, LLDP) to learn devices without scanning. On this container-only install you choose the card it listens on here with Configure.
sensors.descriptionContainer: The sensor listens to the network (DHCP, ARP, mDNS, SSDP, LLDP) to learn devices without scanning. On this container-only install you choose the card it listens on, and the SPAN card, here with Configure.
sensors.off: The passive sensor is off, so Vedette does not discover new devices by itself. Devices you add by hand still work.
sensors.caption: Sensors on this box
sensors.startHint: Start it with compose.sensors.yaml on this machine.
sensors.startingHint: The box is starting the sensor (after setup or after you turned it on). This can take a few minutes; the row updates by itself.
sensors.notStartedHint: The box could not get the sensor running. Turn Passive sensor off and on in Settings → Modules to try again now; on the box, journalctl -u vedette-sensor and journalctl -u vedette-core say why.

capture.label: Capture
capture.no_permission: It cannot open the network card: capturing needs root and CAP_NET_RAW, which a rootless Docker or Podman does not give. Start the sensor as root.
capture.no_interface: The card it should listen on is not on that machine. Choose another card.
capture.filters_invalid: The capture filters cannot be read, so it captures nothing until they change.
capture.capture_failed: The capture keeps failing and is retried; the sensor's log says why.

card.body: Choose the card the sensor listens on among the cards it reported, and whether it is a SPAN card that receives mirrored traffic. This machine's network is yours: Vedette does not change the card.
card.bodyNoSpan: Choose the card the sensor listens on among the cards it reported. This machine's network is yours: Vedette does not change the card.
card.spanKept: {{name}} is saved as a SPAN port. This version of Vedette no longer sets SPAN up: you can untick it, not tick it again.
card.label: Listen on
card.hint: Run ip -br address on this machine to see which card has which address. Choose the card on the network you want to discover.
card.autoChosen: Automatic (the one card of this machine with an address)
card.span: SPAN port: this card receives the switch's mirrored traffic
card.spanHint: Prepare the card on this machine first: no IP address, promiscuous mode, connected to the switch's mirror port.
card.spanNeedsCard: Choose a card under Listen on first: SPAN is set on one named card, not on Automatic.
card.notListening: The sensor is not listening on any card: by itself it only takes the one card of this machine that has an address, and there is not exactly one. Choose the card below.
card.none: No card reported yet: start the sensor with compose.sensors.yaml.

sensors.configBody: The port the sensor listens on and whether mirrored traffic is arriving. Change them in Settings.
sensors.configBodyNoSpan: The port the sensor listens on: the box's management port, set in Settings.
sensors.spanLink: Configure SPAN in Settings → Box network
sensors.spanHint: Vedette reads DNS queries, TLS server names, HTTP hosts and connection metadata from the mirrored traffic to learn devices and spot connections to known-bad addresses. It does not store packet contents. Without mirrored traffic the sensor only sees broadcast messages (DHCP, ARP, mDNS).

agents.title: Agents on servers
agents.description: An agent tells Vedette exactly which software runs on a server, so alerts say "confirmed" instead of "suspected".
agents.recommendation: Use osquery on your Linux and Windows servers. Already run Wazuh? Connect its API instead.
agents.serverOnly: Vedette supports server operating systems only: Linux and Windows Server.

boxAddress.change: Change it in Settings → Box network
boxAddress.container: It is the first name in VEDETTE_HOSTS.
boxAddress.otherHost: You opened Vedette at {{here}}, but agents will use {{box}}.

agents.off: Agent intake is off. Turn this module on to create osquery tokens and connect Wazuh.

osquery.title: osquery on your servers
osquery.intro: Vedette acts as the osquery server. Each machine reports its operating system and installed packages (and Windows hotfixes). osquery only reads; it changes nothing on the machine.

agents.caption: Enrollment tokens
agents.emptyBody: Use "Create agent token", then run the one command it shows on each server.

page.downloadBody: The official osquery {{version}} packages, served by this box. The one command in step 2 downloads the right one by itself; download a package here to copy it to a server yourself (a USB stick works) or to install it with your own tools.
page.checkHint: Before you install, check the file: sha256sum <file> on Linux or Get-FileHash <file> in PowerShell must print the SHA-256 in the table. The package alone reports nothing to Vedette: the agent also needs the token from step 2.
page.none: This box has no copy of the osquery packages, so there is nothing to download here and the one command in step 2 stops at the package download. Update Vedette to the release, which ships them.
page.tokenTitle: 2. Then create a token so the agent can report to this box
page.tokenBody: The token dialog shows the one command that installs osquery from this box and enrolls it, and the manual steps for a package you installed yourself.

agents.configBody: Replace <TOKEN> with the token you saved when you created it. If you lost it, revoke it and create a new one.
agents.sampleHint: Preview build only: there is no backend yet, so this pretends the machines reported in.
agents.sampled: Sample data received: {{devices}} devices updated, {{software}} software entries added from the agent.
agents.revokeBody: Agents using this token are rejected immediately. Data already received is kept.
agents.name: Token name
agents.nameHint: To remember which machines use it, for example "osquery on SRV-AD".
agents.expiryHint: After this the token stops working. You can revoke it earlier.
agents.createdBody: Pick the operating system and run the one command below on the server.
agents.tokenOnce: The token is shown once. After you close this dialog Vedette keeps only the last 4 characters. Copy it somewhere safe first.

noAddress.title: Servers cannot reach this box at the address you opened it with
noAddress.container: You opened Vedette as localhost, and the box knows no other address, so no install command can work yet. Agents need an address of this machine that other machines can reach: in vedette.env put this machine's LAN address in VEDETTE_BIND_IP and that address (or a name that points to it) in VEDETTE_HOSTS, run docker compose --env-file vedette.env up -d again, and open Vedette at that address. The command appears here then.
noAddress.appliance: You opened Vedette as localhost, so this page does not know an address that other machines can reach and no install command can work yet. Open Vedette at the box's network address (Settings → Box network shows it); the command appears here then.
noAddress.token: The token stays valid: keep it, and use it with the command once it appears.

install.title: Install with one command
install.linuxHow: Run as root, or with sudo, on the server (Debian, Ubuntu, RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux; x86_64 or arm64).
install.windowsHow: Run in PowerShell as Administrator on the server (Windows PowerShell 5.1 or later). Not yet tested on a real Windows Server.
install.shaHint: The box uses its own certificate, so the command first downloads the script without trusting it, then refuses to run unless the script's SHA-256 matches the value above. The script carries the box certificate and checks every later download against it. The servers need no Internet: the box serves the osquery package too, after checking its checksum.
install.windowsWhy: Windows PowerShell 5.1 cannot skip certificate checks for a single request, so the command uses curl.exe -k for that one download only, and checks the hash before anything runs.
install.readFirstBody: Read it before you run it. Running it again upgrades or repairs the installation.
install.uninstall: Remove osquery from the server again
install.security: The token can only enroll osquery on a machine and reads nothing from Vedette. It is shown once, expires (7 days by default) and can be revoked. It is sent as an argument and in a header, never in a web address. Every install and enrollment is recorded in the audit log.
install.advancedBody: The same result step by step, for locked-down servers or your own packaging. The package comes from this box and is installed only when its SHA-256 matches the table above. For a file you copied over (USB stick), leave out the download line: on Linux run the first and last lines in the folder that holds the file; on Windows set $f to the file's path, then run the last line.
install.queriesBody: Read-only queries, delivered through the config endpoint. Packages differ per distribution, so each machine runs only the ones that fit it. The interfaces query reports the machine's IPv4 addresses and MAC addresses so Vedette can match it to the right device. In its first hour after enrolling, a machine runs every minute each query whose answer Vedette has not received yet, so its operating system and packages show within a few minutes; it then follows the intervals below. Vedette marks the machine Approved, because whoever made the token vouched for it, and sets its type from its operating system (Windows Server and Linux: Server; other Windows and macOS: PC) unless a person has chosen one.

download.title: Or download the package
download.body: For a server without network access, or to install it your own way: download the official osquery package from this box, copy it to the server (a USB stick works), check its SHA-256 and install it. Then follow the enrollment steps under Advanced: manual setup.
download.caption: osquery packages this box serves
download.none: This box has no copy of the osquery packages for this operating system, so the command below stops at the package download. Update Vedette to the release, which ships them.

linux.installDeb: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it (Debian, Ubuntu)
linux.installRpm: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it (RHEL, Rocky, AlmaLinux)
linux.secret: Save the token and the box certificate, then check the fingerprint

windows.install: Download osquery from the box, check it and install it
windows.secret: Save the token and the box certificate, then check it
windows.service: Install and start the osqueryd service

agents.fingerprint: The downloads in the manual steps use -k, because the box certificate is not trusted yet: the package is installed only when its SHA-256 matches the value on this page, and the certificate step prints its fingerprint for you to compare with the one from your Vedette administrator. osquery verifies the certificate on every later request.
agents.ownPaths: The /api/v1/install/… and /api/v1/intake/… paths are Vedette's own. Everything else follows the osquery and Wazuh documentation.

wazuh.title: Wazuh
wazuh.intro: Already run Wazuh? Vedette reads the agent list, operating systems, installed packages and Windows hotfixes from the Wazuh server API. Nothing is installed on your agent machines, and the Wazuh user can only read.
wazuh.disconnectBody: Vedette stops syncing and deletes the stored password. Data already received stays.

status.never: Connected, waiting for the first sync

wazuh.formBody: Create a read-only API user on the Wazuh manager first (steps below), then enter its details here. Nothing is installed on your agent machines.
wazuh.stepsTitle: 1. Create a read-only API user on the Wazuh manager
wazuh.stepsBody: Run these on a machine that can reach the Wazuh API. The user may only read the agent list and the syscollector inventory (agent:read and syscollector:read).

steps.login: Log in to the Wazuh API
steps.link: Attach the policy to the role and the role to the user

wazuh.urlHint: The Wazuh manager, port 55000 by default, for example https://wazuh-manager:55000.
wazuh.passwordKeep: Leave empty to keep the saved password.
wazuh.passwordHint: Stored encrypted. After saving only the last 4 characters are shown.
wazuh.testOk: Connected to Wazuh {{version}}. This user can see {{count}} agents.

box.title: This is the Vedette box itself
box.lead: It is always the first device.
box.packagesAppliance: Its packages are read from the box (dpkg), so the version list is exact.
box.packagesContainer: The package list of this machine is not available in a container-only install.
box.matched: It is matched against exploited vulnerabilities like any other device.
box.fix: Fix by updating the operating system
box.noDelete: The box cannot be removed from the list: Vedette runs on it.
